payload.title: How does hyp prompt find a Goal body's constraints block?
payload.body: Scenario that separates the rivals: a body with a prose line that starts with Never:, more prose, then a real block of May change:, Read only: and Never: lines. Decided by argument in the grill session; the run builds the winner.

why: A testable option set settled in the grill is still a DesignQuestion with rivals.

payload.title: The block runs from the first heading line to the end of the body
payload.body: From the first column-0 line starting May change:, Read only: or Never: to the end of the body. Every non-empty line in it starts with a heading and all three headings appear. The scenario body is refused with exit 1 and the first failing line is named.

why: Rival A, chosen in the grill: it matches the rule PR #135 wrote in hyp-owner-grill.

payload.title: The block is the trailing run of heading lines
payload.body: The block is the last run of consecutive heading lines at the end of the body; prose before it is ignored. The scenario body is accepted and the real block is printed.

why: Rival B, rejected in the grill: a heading-like line in prose would pass unnoticed and the first failing line could not be named.

payload.title: Scenarios that separate the two block rules, argued in the grill
payload.body: Rule, fixed before the Result: S1 = a body with a prose line starting Never:, a line of prose, then a block of May change:, Read only: and Never: lines. A refuses S1 (exit 1) and names the first failing line, which is the prose line after the first Never:. B accepts S1 and prints the trailing block. S2 = a body that is only a valid block: both accept. S3 = a block followed by a prose line: A refuses, B accepts. The owner chose A in the session because a heading-like line in prose must not pass unnoticed. Verdicts: A supports on S1 and S3; B contradicts. Evidence: the scenarios file.

why: Records the rival choice as argued, not tested.

payload.observation: Records the grill's argued choice under the Experiment's pre-registered rule: the owner chose rule A in session; S1 and S3 separate the rivals and rule B fails the refusal case.

why: The argued block-rule question moves to its own design-record Goal: a Goal with lines owes every line on it, and no run can cover them. Owner chose this in the grill.
